claims: Ichthyotitan severnensis is a newly identified species of giant Triassic ichthyosaur.
Ichthyotitan severnensis means "giant fish lizard of the Severn".
Ichthyotitan severnensis is roughly 25 meters long.
Ruby Reynolds was 11 years old at the time of the discovery.
Ruby Reynolds and her father Justin Reynolds discovered the second, more complete jawbone piece (surangular) in May 2020 at Blue Anchor, Somerset.
Paul de la Salle found an initial large bone fragment in 2016 at Lilstock.
The 2020 jawbone fragments matched the 2016 find by Paul de la Salle.
Dr. Dean Lomax, along with researchers from the University of Bristol and Manchester, compared the new find with the 2016 piece.
Dr. Dean Lomax and the researchers confirmed the finds as a new genus and species.
The fossils date to about 202 million years ago.
The fossils are from the Late Triassic.
The jawbone measures over 2 meters in length.
The findings were formally published in 2024 in the journal PLoS ONE.
The fossils are destined for display at the Bristol Museum and Art Gallery
